title: Sell Mineral Rights in Ellenboro, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Ellenboro, WV | Ritchie County
metaDescription: Ellenboro, WV sits in historic Ritchie County oil country with modern Marcellus leasing layered on top. We buy mineral interests directly, no obligation.
heroLead: Ellenboro sits along US Route 50 in Ritchie County, a small town built next to some of the earliest commercial oil production in the country, and its mineral tracts have been leased in some form for well over a hundred years.
intro: Like much of Ritchie County, Ellenboro's ground carries shallow Big Injun and Gordon sand production dating back generations, with modern Marcellus and Utica/Point Pleasant leasing added on top over the last fifteen years. That combination means a single tract can have more than one operator paying royalty under more than one lease.

We buy mineral and royalty interests around Ellenboro directly, reading the actual recorded lease and unit history for your tract before making an offer, since the shallow and deep interests here rarely share the same terms.

sections.heading: Old wells still on the books
paragraphs: It's common near Ellenboro to find a shallow well still nominally producing, or held on a shut-in status, under a lease signed decades ago. That lease can remain legally active even with minimal current production, which affects how we evaluate the interest.

sections.heading: Checking for flat-rate lease terms
paragraphs: Older Ritchie County leases sometimes pay a fixed annual sum instead of a share of production value. We check whether an Ellenboro-area lease qualifies for West Virginia's statutory conversion to a minimum one-eighth royalty before pricing the interest.

sections.heading: Generations of heirs on the same tract
paragraphs: With this much history behind a lease, ownership has typically split multiple times over. We regularly work with Ellenboro-area interests held by eight or more heirs and buy individual fractional shares without requiring the whole family to sell together.

It's also common for one heir to have quietly kept collecting a small legacy check while cousins elsewhere never knew the interest existed. Confirming everyone's actual share is part of the work we do before pricing your piece of it.

faqs.question: My family's Ellenboro well hasn't produced in years. Is the lease still active?
faqs.answer: It can be, if the lease has a shut-in clause or minimal continuing production. We check the specific lease terms and well status before evaluating your interest.

faqs.question: Do I get paid separately for a legacy well and a newer Marcellus well?
faqs.answer: Yes, if both cover your tract and are active, each pays under its own lease or unit order.

faqs.question: How do you handle an interest with many co-owners?
faqs.answer: We can purchase an individual heir's share directly without requiring the rest of the family to participate in the sale.
